title: Quantile-Free Uncertainty Quantification in Graph Neural Networks
claim: A dual-head model trained with a joint loss balancing two opposing terms yields tighter, adaptive uncertainty intervals than a single term alone.
layout: Left-to-right pipeline, then two stacked plots feeding a large arrow to result plot
description: The figure reads left to right. At far left is a small graph G with grey node-feature bars. An arrow labeled (V, E) leads into a stacked GNN block. The GNN feeds two yellow-rounded LINEAR heads, one for ŷ and one for d̂. These produce orange feature vectors, which cross over into blue upper and lower bound vectors (ŷ^up, ŷ^low). Dashed lines run from the bounds into a light-blue Joint Loss box, and a dashed backpropagation arrow returns to the GNN. Two boxes sit to the right: a blue-outlined L_coverage box and a red-outlined L_width box, joined by a double arrow. Beside them, two small scatter plots show the coverage-only intervals (too wide) and the width-only intervals (collapsed). A big blue arrow points to a final plot. It shows tight, adaptive light-blue intervals around the points, with red and blue arrows marking the width and coverage forces.
caption: Overview of Quantile-free Prediction Interval Graph Neural Network. QpiGNN estimates node-wise prediction intervals using a dual-head GNN trained with a quantile-free joint loss that trades off coverage and compactness. One head predicts the target value ˆy, while the other predicts the interval width ˆd. The loss includes a coverage term Lcoverage (û) encouraging wide enough intervals to maintain coverage, and a width term Lwidth (ø) promoting tighter intervals. As illustrated, models trained with only the coverage term produce overly wide intervals, whereas the full joint loss yields tighter, locally adaptive intervals that still satisfy the target coverage 1 −α.
abstract: Uncertainty quantification (UQ) in graph neural networks (GNNs) is crucial in high-stakes domains but remains a significant challenge. In graph settings, message passing often relies on strong assumptions such as exchangeability, which are rarely satisfied in practice, and achieving reliable UQ typically requires costly resampling or post-hoc calibration. To address these issues, we introduce Quantile-free Prediction Interval GNN (QpiGNN), a framework that builds on quantile regression (QR) to enable GNN-based UQ by directly optimizing coverage and interval width without requiring quantile inputs or post-processing. QpiGNN employs a dual-head architecture that decouples prediction and uncertainty, and is trained with label-only supervision through a quantile-free joint loss. This design allows efficient training and yields robust prediction intervals, with theoretical guarantees of asymptotic coverage and near-optimal width under mild assumptions. Experiments on 19 synthetic and real-world benchmarks show QpiGNN achieves average 22% higher coverage and 50% narrower intervals than baselines, while ensuring efficiency and robustness to noise and structural shifts.
